What to look for in leather jackets

  • Laminated beats drop-liner. A bonded waterproof membrane keeps the outer from soaking through and chilling you in sustained rain.
  • CE Level 2 armour. Insist on shoulder and elbow protectors, and budget for a back protector if one is not included.
  • Layering system. A removable thermal liner turns one jacket into a three-season solution for British weather.
  • Connection zip. A jacket-to-trouser zip stops your kit separating in a slide — buy matching pieces where possible.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on leather jackets?

Our catalogue spans £99.99 to £809.99. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Alpinestars, Ixon, Richa, Rebelhorn, RST, Oxford. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Textile or leather?

Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport touring. Many riders own both.

faq.a: Leather offers the best abrasion resistance of any common material, which is why race suits are made from it. In a slide it resists wearing through longer than most textiles. However, safety also depends on CE-rated construction and armour, and modern high-end textiles are very capable too. Leather's edge is greatest in high-speed sport and track riding rather than everyday commuting.

A one-piece suit, such as the Alpinestars GP Force V2 or Ixon Vortex 3, gives the best protection and aerodynamics for track days and fast sport riding because it cannot ride up or separate. A leather jacket like the RST S1 CE or Rebelhorn Veloce is far more practical for road use, pairing with jeans or leather trousers via a connection zip.

faq.q: Is leather any good in UK rain?
faq.a: Leather is not waterproof. It soaks up water, becomes heavy and cold and takes a long time to dry, and repeated soakings can harden it if not cared for. For wet UK touring a laminated textile jacket is the better tool. Leather is best kept for dry days, and many riders carry a waterproof over-jacket for unexpected showers.

faq.q: How do I care for a leather jacket?
faq.a: Let a wet jacket dry naturally away from direct heat, which would crack the leather, then apply a leather conditioner to keep it supple. Wipe off road grime regularly and store it on a broad hanger away from damp. Well cared for, quality leather lasts for many years and often outlives several textile jackets.

faq.q: Should leather fit tighter than textile?
faq.a: Yes, leather should fit snugly so the armour stays over your shoulders and elbows and does not shift in a slide, and it will give slightly as it beds in and moulds to you. It should feel close but not restrict movement in a riding crouch. A slightly firm fit when new is normal, whereas a roomy leather jacket compromises protection.
